title: Improved Sealing of the Flap Track Carriage Roller Bearings
abstract: A double-lip seal and a revised grease specification are introduced on the flap track carriage roller bearings to stop runway contaminant reaching the raceway, after a cluster of rough-running findings on de-icing networks.

sections.reason: Operators in northern networks reported rough flap running and, in eleven cases across five aircraft, carriage roller replacement at unscheduled maintenance. Grease samples taken from four returned carriages showed chloride concentrations consistent with runway de-icing fluid, and two raceways showed early spalling. The single-lip seal fitted to the original carriage does not exclude a fine aerosol driven by the wheel spray pattern at rotation, which the flap track drainage arrangement then holds against the seal face.
sections.description: The carriage roller bearings receive a double-lip seal with a garter spring and are packed with a grease qualified against chloride washout. The carriage actuator assembly D2750130352279 is retained; the filter assembly D2750139843846 in the track drain path is replaced by a coarser item that clears wet debris instead of trapping it, and the heat exchanger BEDE63136-96 mounting is re-shimmed by 1.5 mm to keep the drain slope. Countersunk rivets EN207383K8 close the revised seal retainer. Detail is on drawing D27500031461. Work is done in the flap areas, zones 562 and 662, with the flaps at the maintenance position. The regulator 5CE and the track valve 9KS3 are disturbed and refitted unchanged.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 2.2 kg per aircraft across all carriages. No electrical load change. Interchangeable, and operators may change carriages individually as they become due. The carriage lubrication interval extends from 3 000 to 6 000 flight hours and the rough-running functional check is deleted. Two aircraft on an extended flight-test loan are excluded because they carry an instrumented carriage that this modification would disturb.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00364 in October 2021. Retrofit is through Service Bulletin MRD-27-1078, done one wing at a time inside a scheduled C-check; operators normally combine it with the flap track lubrication task so that the flaps only have to be driven once.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN M00364, supplier carriage build standard change
